newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian dollar ends firm in narrow range-trade.
newsitem.headline: Canadian dollar ends firm in narrow range-trade.

text.p: Canada's dollar ended firmer at C$1.3855 (US$0.7217) on Tuesday from Monday's close of C$1.3892 (US$0.7198) in narrow range-trading, dealers said. * They said the currency enjoyed a relatively narrow range because market players were split over the possibility of a U.S. interest rate rise at next week's FOMC meeting.
Farrill said all eyes were focused on U.S. economic data due out this week.
The U.S. government is expected to report the nation's April producer prices on Wednesday and consumer prices on Thursday, both indicators of inflationary pressure in the economy.
"The markets are really quite keen to see CPI and PPI over the next two days," Farrill said.
Analysts said the Canadian dollar could turn sharply weaker if the economic data pointed to rising inflationary pressures and increased the likelihood of a U.S. rate hike.

"The news is particularly sensitive to Canadian markets in that a Fed hike will lead to a weaker Canadian dollar and possibly higher short-term rates," said Jeoff Hall, Canadian Market Analyst for Technical Data in Boston.

A Reuter survey of economists forecast April producer prices would be reported unchanged, compared to a fall of 0.1 percent in the previous period. It also forecast consumer prices in April would rise 0.1 percent, compared to 0.1 percent in the previous period. On the crosses, Canada's dollar rose to 85.48 yen from Monday's close of 85.86 yen and slipped to 1.2209 marks from Monday's 1.2284 marks.
